facts.statement: The genus Probrachylophosaurus was described by Freedman Fowler and Horner in 2015.
facts.quote: authority: Freedman Fowler & Horner, 2015

facts.statement: Fossils of Probrachylophosaurus date to the Campanian age between 80.45 and 79 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in rocks of the Judith River Formation in Montana and the Foremost Formation in Alberta, and date to the Campanian age, 80.45–79 million years ago.

facts.statement: The first fossils of Probrachylophosaurus were discovered in Montana in 1981, but the skeleton was not fully excavated until 2008.
facts.quote: First discovered in Montana in 1981 and not fully excavated until 2008

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus was a large, four-legged herbivore about 10 meters long with a large beak.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaur, Probrachylophosaurus would have been a large herbivore, 10 m in length, that walked primarily on four legs and possessed a large beak.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus had a short, paddle-shaped head crest formed by an extension of the nasal bone.
facts.quote: In Probrachylophosaurus this crest is a short, paddle-shaped extension of the nasal bone projecting over the back of the head.

facts.statement: Evidence of injuries, including fractured tail vertebrae, suggests Probrachylophosaurus may have interacted aggressively with other hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: The most complete specimen possesses several injuries, including a series of fractured tail vertebrae that may have been damaged by interactions with other hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: Histologic analysis indicates that Probrachylophosaurus experienced fast growth rates similar to other hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Histologic analysis indicates fast growth, similar to other hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: Comparisons with Maiasaura suggest Probrachylophosaurus took approximately twice as long to reach sexual maturity.
facts.quote: However, comparisons with the related Maiasaura indicate that Probrachylophosaurus took around twice as long to reach sexual maturity.

facts.statement: The oldest known specimen of Probrachylophosaurus was about 14 years old and had reached over 95% of its adult size at death.
facts.quote: The oldest known specimen had likely reached over 95% of its adult size upon death at 14 years of age, but did not yet show signs of complete skeletal maturity.

facts.statement: The specific name 'bergei' honors Sam Berge, a landowner who supported the research.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Sam Berge, one of the landowners, and his friends who have supported the research.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus was one of eighteen dinosaur taxa described in 2015 in open access or free-to-read journals.
facts.quote: Probrachylophosaurus was one of eighteen dinosaur taxa from 2015 to be described in open access or free-to-read journals.

facts.statement: In 2021, three fragmentary specimens from the Foremost Formation were referred to the genus Probrachylophosaurus, but not to the species P. bergei.
facts.quote: In 2021, three specimens from the upper layers of the Foremost Formation were referred to the genus Probrachylophosaurus, though not to P. bergei.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the specimen Brachylophosaurus goodwini is a distinct species or merely a younger specimen of Probrachylophosaurus bergei.
facts.quote: However, a 2021 paper studying growth in the genus Maiasaura noted these traits, relating to the depth of depressions on the frontal, could vary over the lifespan of hadrosaurs. Therefore, they considered it possible that B. goodwini merely represented a younger specimen of P. bergei.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus is thought to be a close relative of Brachylophosaurus and Ornatops and a possible descendant of Acristavus.
facts.quote: Thought to be a close relative of the later Brachylophosaurus and Ornatops, and a possible descendant of the older Acristavus, it represents a possible transitional state in brachylophosaurin evolution.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus was a large quadrupedal hadrosaur with slender front limbs, strong hind limbs, and a long stiff tail.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaur, Probrachylophosaurus would have been a large quadrupedal animal with gracile forelimbs, longer more robust hindlimbs, and a long, tall horizontal tail stiffened by ossified tendons.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Probrachylophosaurus is the largest known member of the brachysaurolophine group.
facts.quote: A large hadrosaur, the holotype is the largest brachysaurolophin specimen known.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus is estimated to have reached a length of 10 meters.
facts.quote: Its size has been estimated at 10 m in length.

facts.statement: The holotype individual weighed approximately 4.3 metric tons at death, representing near maximum size for the species.
facts.quote: Body mass estimate suggests that the holotype was 4.3 MT at time of death, and was close to maximum size.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus exhibits an intermediate anatomical condition between the earlier crestless Acristavus and the later Brachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: In particular, Probrachylophosaurus shows a distinctly intermediate condition between the anatomy of the earlier crestless relative Acristavus and its possible descendant Brachylophosaurus.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus possessed a large beak at the front of its mouth, a trait shared with other hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: The front of the mouth would have borne a large beak, as in other hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: The lower jaw beak of Probrachylophosaurus was formed by a predentary bone that was roughly twice as wide as it was long, featuring squared-off front corners.
facts.quote: On the lower jaw, the beak was formed by the predentary bone, which was roughly twice as wide as long with squared off front corners.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Probrachylophosaurus featured a short toothless section at the front followed by prominent dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth.
facts.quote: Each dentary had a downward sloping toothless section at the front and prominent dental batteries with hundreds of teeth farther back.

facts.statement: The most distinguishing feature of Probrachylophosaurus is a solid, paddle-shaped crest formed by the paired nasal bones projecting above the skull.
facts.quote: The most distinguishing aspect of Probrachylophosaurus is its solid paddle-shaped crest formed by the paired left and right nasal bones projecting above the back of the skull.

facts.statement: Unlike the flat crest of Brachylophosaurus, the crest of Probrachylophosaurus is raised in the center, forming a triangular cross-section with an angle of 112 degrees in the known adult specimen.
facts.quote: Unlike the relatively flat crest of Brachylophosaurus, that of Probrachylophosaurus is raised in the centre, forming a triangular cross section with the top points forming an angle of less than 130° (112° in the known adult specimen).

facts.statement: The crest of Probrachylophosaurus ends in a V-shape, contrasting with the U-shape found in Brachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: The end of the crest terminates in a v-shape, unlike the u-shape of Brachylophosaurus.

facts.statement: In Probrachylophosaurus, the frontals covering the nasal attachment area cover only about 59% of the frontal bone, compared to full coverage in adult Brachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: While in adult Brachylophosaurus these cover the entire top of the frontal to support the longer crest, in Probrachylophosaurus they only cover around half of the frontal (59% coverage).

facts.statement: The quadrate bones in Probrachylophosaurus are straight in shape, unlike those in Brachylophosaurus and Maiasaura where the top half leans backward.
facts.quote: The left and right quadrate form the rear corners of each side of the skull. In Probrachylophosaurus and Acristavus the quadrates are straight in shape, whereas the top half leans backward in Brachylophosaurus and Maiasaura.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus is a solid-crested hadrosaur belonging to the subfamily Saurolophinae and the tribe Brachylophosaurini.
facts.quote: Probrachylophosaurus is a hadrosaur, belonging to the solid-crested subfamily Saurolophinae (alternatively Hadrosaurinae) and specifically to a lineage known as Brachylophosaurini.

facts.statement: Early phylogenetic analyses disagreed on whether Probrachylophosaurus was a close relative of Brachylophosaurus or a sister taxon to a group containing both Brachylophosaurus and Maiasaura.
facts.quote: In the former, Probrachylophosaurus was found to be the sister taxon to a grouping of Brachylophosaurus and Maiasaura. Contrastingly, the latter found Probrachylophosaurus and Brachylophosaurus to be sister taxa, with Maiasaura as an outgroup to the two.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus possessed a wide, backward-projecting head crest supported by long striations along the frontal and nasal bones.
facts.quote: The former three are united by the anatomy of the suture of the frontals and nasals, which consists of long striations along the frontals expanded backwards to support the wide, backward projecting head crest known from Probrachylophosaurus and Brachylophosaurus (and inferred to be present in Ornatops).

facts.statement: Unlike Probrachylophosaurus, the crest of the related genus Maiasaura had a different structure and did not project backward over the skull.
facts.quote: Maiasaura also possesses a crest, but it is very different in structure and does not project over the back skull.

facts.statement: A specific specimen of Probrachylophosaurus reached an age of fourteen years when it died.
facts.quote: In the tested specimen of Probrachylophosaurus MOR 2919, fourteen LAGs indicated the animal was fourteen years of age at death.

facts.statement: The display crest on the head of Probrachylophosaurus grew significantly later in life than the rest of the skeleton.
facts.quote: Unlike the rest of the body, the display crest on the top of the head experiences much of its growth very late in the life history of the animal.

facts.statement: Sexual maturity in Probrachylophosaurus appears to have been reached at approximately five years of age.
facts.quote: In MOR 2919, this appears to happen at five years of age.

facts.statement: A fourteen-year-old Probrachylophosaurus specimen had reached 95% of its maximum size by the age of nine.
facts.quote: By nine years of age, MOR 2919 had reached 95% of its size at death.

facts.statement: Studies indicate Probrachylophosaurus had a maximum growth rate of 855 kg per year between the ages of 3.64 and 4.64 years.
facts.quote: A later 2020 study on hadrosaur growth reanalyzed Probrachylophosaurus and Maiasaura, finding the former to have a maximum growth rate between 3.64 and 4.64 years of age, growing 855 kg per year at that point in life.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of the Probrachylophosaurus type specimen shows three circular depressions surrounded by raised bone rings.
facts.quote: Across the dentaries, three circular depressions can be seen surrounded by rings of raised bone.

facts.statement: Six vertebrae in the middle of the tail of the Probrachylophosaurus type specimen show healed breakage across their neural spines.
facts.quote: Six of the vertebrae from the middle of the tail show breakage and healing across their neural spines.

facts.statement: Scientists have proposed multiple causes for tail injuries in hadrosaurs, including predator attacks, herd trampling, biomechanical stress, and mating behavior.
facts.quote: Various proposals have been made for their cause including attacks from predators, other members of their herds stepping on their tails, biomechanical stress, and damage occurring in females due to being mounted by males during mating.

facts.statement: Recent research suggests that mating behavior, specifically mounting by males, is the most likely cause of the healed tail injuries found in Probrachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: A 2026 study found the mating mechanism to be most likely and ruled out the other hypotheses as failing to explain the pattern of damage seen across hadrosaurs specimens.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus lived between 80.45 and 79.5 million years ago during the early Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Fossils belonging to Probrachylophosaurus were deposited between 80.45 and 79.5 million years ago in the early Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: The environment where Probrachylophosaurus lived is interpreted as a fluvial floodplain ecosystem.
facts.quote: This section is thought to represent a fluvial floodplain ecosystem.

facts.statement: Fossilized gut contents indicate that Probrachylophosaurus ate leaves, consistent with other hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Fossilized gut contents from Brachylophosaurus indicate a diet of leaves, consistent with widers studies on the diet of hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus is estimated to have reached a length of nine meters and a weight of over five tonnes.
facts.quote: Su longitud se ha estimado en nueve metros, con un peso de más de cinco toneladas.

facts.statement: Due to its large size, the holotype fossil of Probrachylophosaurus was nicknamed "Super-Duck".
facts.quote: Debido a su tamaño el fósil fue apodado como "Super-Duck" (superpato).

facts.statement: The skull crest of Probrachylophosaurus is formed entirely by large nasal bones that overlap the supratemporal fenestra by less than two centimeters in adults.
facts.quote: La cresta craneal se compone de un hueso grande y está formada enteramente por los huesos nasales los cuales, en los individuos adultos, se superponen a la fenestra supratemporal por una distancia de menos de dos centímetros.

facts.statement: The crest is thickened in the middle, causing the posterior frontal bones to grow more with an acute triangular cross-section and a superior posterior angle of less than 130 degrees.
facts.quote: Esta cresta se encuentra muy engrosada en la mitad, lo que resulta en que la posición posterior de los huesos frontales este crece de más, con una sección transversal aguda y triangular, cuyo ángulo superior en vista posterior es de menos de 130°.

facts.statement: The posterior part of the lacrimal bone is transversely wide, a trait shared with Acristavus but not with Brachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: La parte posterior del hueso lacrimal es transversalmente ancha como ocurre en Acristavus pero no en Brachylophosaurus.

facts.statement: In the frontal ramus of the jugal, the lower corner is positioned behind the level of the upper corner, a feature found in Acristavus but not in Brachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: En el ramo frontal del yugal, la esquina inferior se posiciona detrás del nivel de la esquina superior, como en Acristavus pero no Brachylophosaurus.

facts.statement: The squamosals touch at the midline of the skull, a characteristic present in Acristavus but absent in Probrachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: Los escamosales se tocan en la línea media del cráneo como en Acristavus pero no en Brachylophosaurus.

facts.statement: The nasal bone of the crest is large, nearly horizontal, and directed backward, a trait shared with Brachylophosaurus but different from Acristavus.
facts.quote: El hueso nasal de la cresta es grande y casi horizontal y dirigida hacia atrás como en Brachylophosaurus y a diferencia de Acristavus.

facts.statement: The genus Probrachylophosaurus was named by Freedman, Fowler, and Horner in 2015.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Freedman Fowler & Horner, 2015

facts.statement: The only known species of Probrachylophosaurus is P. bergei.
facts.quote: species: P. bergei

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus bergei is the only known species of the extinct genus Probrachylophosaurus, a braquilofosaurine hadrosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Probrachylophosaurus bergei es la única especie conocida del género extinto Probrachylophosaurus de dinosaurio hadrosáurido braquilofosaurino

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus is considered a transitional genus between Acristavus and Brachylophosaurus, evolving from a crestless ancestor to a crested descendant while changing nasal bone morphology.
facts.quote: La importancia de este hadrosáurido en particular reside en que es un género transicional entre los géneros Acristavus y Brachylophosaurus, evolucionando de un ancestro sin cresta (el primer género) a un descendiente con cresta (el último) mientras cambiaba la morfología de sus huesos nasales.

facts.statement: The discovery of Probrachylophosaurus suggests that brachylophosaurs were among the first hadrosaurs to colonize fluvial lowlands after the Claggett Seaway receded.
facts.quote: The discovery of Probrachylophosaurus in the Foremost Formation indicates brachylophosaurs were amongst the first hadrosaurs to colonize the fluvial lowlands following the recession of the Claggett Seaway.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the evolution of brachylophosaurs was driven by habitat preference, with some suggesting a divergence from an upland ancestor to suit coastal lowland ecosystems.
facts.quote: The evolution of brachylophosaurs has been proposed to be linked to habitat preference. Maiasaura is primarily known from inland, upland Two Medicine deposits, whereas Brachylophosaurus is known from the coastal lowlands of the Judith River Formation.

facts.statement: The idea that dinosaur faunas were environmentally sensitive is challenged by evidence showing similar dinosaurs lived in diverse environments.
facts.quote: The concept of environmental sensitivity amongst dinosaur faunas has been challenged, with analysis of dinosaur microfossil records indicating that similar dinosaurs lived across a variety of environments.

facts.statement: Researchers argue that despite challenges to environmental sensitivity, habitat preference may still have driven the evolution of hadrosaurs like Brachylophosaurini because microfossils cannot distinguish fine taxonomic differences.
facts.quote: However, it has been argued that because microfossils such as teeth cannot detect fine taxonomic distinctions (as related species would share dental anatomy), it remains plausible that habitat preference was a driver of the evolution of hadrosaurs such as the members of Brachylophosaurini.

facts.statement: The partial overlap of Maiasaura and Brachylophosaurus in the Oldman Formation suggests a more complex evolutionary scenario than simple habitat-driven divergence.
facts.quote: Nonetheless, the discovery that Maiasaura and Brachylophosaurus at least partially overlapped in range in the Oldman Formation indicates a potentially more complex scenario.

facts.statement: Mark Goodwin excavated limb bones and a vertebra near Rudyard in northern Montana in 1981 and 1994.
facts.quote: En 1981 y 1994, Mark Goodwin del Museo de Paleontología de la Universidad de California excavó huesos de extremidades y una vértebra cerca de Rudyard en el norte de Montana

facts.statement: The fossil remains were donated to the Museum of the Rockies by landowners Nolan and Cheryl Fladstol, and John and Claire Wendland.
facts.quote: El fósil fue donado al Museo de las Rocosas por los propietarios del terreno, Nolan y Cheryl Fladstol, y John y Claire Wendland.

facts.statement: The type species Probrachylophosaurus bergei was named and described by Elizabeth A. Freedman Fowler and Jack Horner in 2015.
facts.quote: En 2015, la especie tipo Probrachylophosaurus bergei fue nombrada y descrita por Elizabeth A. Freedman Fowler y Jack Horner.

facts.statement: The genus name combines the Latin word for "before" with Brachylophosaurus, indicating its lower stratigraphic position relative to its relative.
facts.quote: El nombre del género es una combinación del latín pro, "antes de", y Brachylophosaurus, en referencia a que este género se sitúa en una posición estratigráfica inferior con respecto a su pariente Brachylophosaurus.

facts.statement: The species name honors Sam Berge, one of the landowners, and his friends who supported the research.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie es en honor de Sam Berge, uno de los terratenientes, y sus amigos quienes apoyaron la investigación.

facts.statement: The holotype MOR 2919 was found in the Judith River Formation dating to the late Campanian, between 79.8 and 79.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MOR 2919, fue hallado en una capa de la Formación Río Judith que data de fines del Campaniense, hace entre 79.8 a 79.5 millones de años

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton with a skull of an adult individual.
facts.quote: Consiste de un esqueleto parcial con cráneo de un individuo adulto.

facts.statement: The bones were not found articulated.
facts.quote: Los huesos no fueron hallados articulados.

facts.statement: Specimen MOR 1097, a fragmentary skull of a subadult individual, was referred to this species and found one kilometer from the holotype.
facts.quote: El espécimen MOR 1097, un cráneo fragmentario de un individuo subadulto, fue referido a esta especie. Fue encontrado a un kilómetro de distancia del holotipo.

facts.statement: The authors of its description placed Probrachylophosaurus in the subfamily Saurolophinae and the tribe Brachylophosaurini.
facts.quote: Probrachylophosaurus fue situado en la subfamilia Saurolophinae y en la tribu Brachylophosaurini por los autores de su descripción.

facts.statement: In one analysis it was recovered as the sister genus to Brachylophosaurus, while in another it was the sister genus to a clade consisting of Brachylophosaurus and Maiasaura.
facts.quote: En un análisis fue recuperado como el género hermano de Brachylophosaurus; en otro como el género hermano de un clado consistente en Brachylophosaurus y Maiasaura.

facts.statement: The authors suggested that Acristavus may have been the direct ancestor of Probrachylophosaurus, which in turn was the ancestor of Brachylophosaurus, which lived about 1.5 million years later.
facts.quote: Los autores sugirieron que Acristavus puede haber sido el ancestro directo de Probrachylophosaurus y este último, en vista de su cresta pequeña intermedia, siendo a su vez ancestro de Brachylophosaurus el cual vivió unos 1.5 millones de años más tarde.

facts.statement: The left tibia showed fourteen lines of arrested growth, which likely represent annual seasons of poor food consumption.
facts.quote: Este hueso mostró catorce líneas de crecimiento detenido, que probablemente representan las estaciones anuales de escaso consumo de comida.

facts.statement: Therefore, the age of the holotype could be around fourteen years old.
facts.quote: Por tanto la edad del holotipo podría ser de alrededor de catorce años.

facts.statement: The lines also show a general slowing of growth after the fifth year, which could indicate that sexual maturity was reached at that age.
facts.quote: Las líneas también muestran una ralentización general del crecimiento tras el quinto año. Esto podría ser una indicación de que la madurez sexual se alcanzaba a esa edad.
